---

## 1. Problem & Context

**What problem does this solve?**
Notebook export writes one notebook's cells, with each cell's output beside it, to a single file that opens without the notebook app. It matters because a notebook's results can only be seen inside the app today, so there is no single document to hand to someone who needs to see what the notebook did.

**Who is affected?**
- Notebook authors, typically data analysts: to share results they take screenshots or copy cells into a separate document by hand.
- Colleagues who receive shared results: they get screenshots or hand-made copies that go stale as soon as the notebook is re-run.
- The maintainer: signs off on this feature.

**What exists today?**
There is no export. Results are shared as screenshots or as cells copied by hand into another document, and those copies stop matching the notebook the moment it is re-run.

---

## 2. Scope

**In Scope:**
- Export one notebook's cells and their outputs to a single file.
- Place each output directly after the cell that produced it, in the notebook's cell order.
- Produce a file that can be opened and read without the notebook app installed.

**Out of Scope:**
- Editing the exported file.
- Exporting more than one notebook at a time.
- Uploading the exported file to any cloud service or shared drive.
- Any export format other than the one chosen for the first release.

---

## 3. Units of Work

- **Unit 1 (Urgent):** Export a notebook and its text outputs to one shareable file. A notebook author exports a single notebook and gets one file holding every cell in order, each followed by its saved text output, that a colleague can read without the notebook app; the other units extend this export.
- **Unit 2 (High):** Include image and chart outputs in the exported file. Charts and images a cell produced appear beside that cell inside the same file, so colleagues see visual results without screenshots.
- **Unit 3 (Medium):** Mark outputs the export cannot show. When a cell's output cannot be shown in the exported format, the file says so in that output's place, so a reader is never misled by a silently incomplete document.

**Happy path:** Author saves the notebook → runs the export on that notebook → receives one file → sends it to a colleague → colleague opens it without the notebook app and reads each cell with its output beside it

---

## 4. Requirements

Each ID below is a functional requirement number (FR); the tracker issue that covers a requirement cites its ID.

| ID | Description | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------------|----------|---------------------|
| FR-001 | Export one notebook to a single file | Urgent | Exporting a saved notebook produces exactly one file. The file contains every cell of that notebook, code and text cells alike, in the notebook's order. |
| FR-002 | Place each cell's saved output directly after that cell | Urgent | Each output appears immediately after the cell that produced it and before the next cell. A cell with no output is followed directly by the next cell. The outputs are the ones saved in the notebook when the export runs; the export does not re-run any cell. |
| FR-003 | The exported file opens without the notebook app | Urgent | On a machine without the notebook app installed, the file opens and every cell and text output in it is readable. |
| FR-004 | Include image and chart outputs beside their cells | High | An image or chart produced by a cell appears in the file directly after that cell and can be viewed without the notebook app. The image is carried inside the exported file, so the export is still one file. |
| FR-005 | Show a note in place of any output the export cannot show | Medium | When a cell's output is of a kind the exported format cannot display, the file shows a short note in that output's position naming the kind of output left out. The rest of the notebook still exports. |

**Design-system components:**
- Not applicable: this feature is not UI-facing.

**Key constraints:**
- Single file: everything a reader needs, including images, is inside the one exported file.
- Faithful to the saved run: [ASSUMPTION] "reflects the run it was exported from" means the export uses the outputs saved in the notebook at export time and never re-runs cells.

## Open Questions

- [ ] Which file format the first release exports to, for example HTML or PDF. Owner: the maintainer, before build starts, because the acceptance checks for FR-003 and FR-004 depend on it. Target date not set.
- [ ] Which notebook file format the export reads. [ASSUMPTION] Jupyter-style notebook files, which store each cell's outputs with the cell. Owner: the maintainer, before build starts.
- [ ] How a notebook author starts an export. [ASSUMPTION] A command run from a terminal, since the feature is not UI-facing. Owner: the maintainer, before build starts.

The maintainer owns all three decisions above and needs to make them before build starts.
